description: Structured screening criteria (ADR-0012) and their hand-written labels, for measuring services/cv_facts and services/structured_match -- the engine that answers the product's default path. The existing jobs.json and labels.json measure the older profile-and-model path, which is now the exception. Every verdict here was read from the candidate's own CV text and from the criterion's stated meaning; none was copied from the engine's output, because a label taken from the thing under test measures nothing. The `candidates` block below holds documents this dataset owns: CVs added to exercise reading rather than scoring, whose shape -- a two-column flattening, Indonesian headings, organisational sections, misspellings -- is the shape real uploads arrive in. They are not in candidates.json because the legacy path would then need profile items and thirteen more labels each, all measuring code ADR-0012 demoted.

candidates.purpose: A school leaver's two-column CV, as extraction actually delivers it: the page is flattened into one stream of lines, so the sidebar and the main narrative interleave and every heading lands away from the entries under it. Also carries the two sections a screener must not read as employment -- a student council post and a one-off event committee -- and a work entry dated as a month range inside a single year.
cv_text: Melayani pembelian dan mencatat transaksi harian.

candidates.purpose: An ordinary Indonesian accounting CV and the strong match of this set. Entirely in Indonesian, with year-only date ranges, the dates on their own lines as a right-aligned column flattens them, and an Indonesian grade line. Nothing here is adversarial: it is the shape the product is actually for.

candidates.purpose: The same CV a candidate typed in a hurry. 'Akutansi' for 'Akuntansi' and 'Micrsoft' for 'Microsoft' are the two misspellings this author has seen most often on real Indonesian CVs. A human reads straight through both; the screener matches surface forms, so this is where that costs the candidate. Labelled as a human reads it, which is the point.

candidates.purpose: A final-year student: a degree being read towards rather than held, one accounting internship, and a treasurer's post in a student society. Three distinctions in one document -- an expected degree is not a degree, an internship is an internship and not a job, and a society office is not employment -- each of which a screener that guesses gets wrong in the candidate's favour.
